messages:
maria: hey team — noticed a weird spike in token charges for a small canary yesterday, looks like some toolcalls got double-counted after a route alias rewrite :thinking:
leo: any traces or console links? :eyes:
maria: https://console.redwood.internal/customer/ACME/trace/abc123 — you'll see two meter events for the same session/toolcall id around 13:42 UTC
maria: quick snippet from the trace event: ```json
{
  "session_id": "s-42f",
  "toolcall_id": "tc-7",
  "route_alias": "wildcard/* -> model-v2",
  "phase": "streaming",
  "action": "truncate_and_fallback",
  "tokens_charged": 120
}
```
ida: hmm looks like the router handoff path adds a synthetic toolcall record when aliasing triggers fallback. we recently added alias-preserve heuristics, maybe it's creating an extra accounting event
mike: that would align with my deploy last week — I merged enable-alias-handoff (commit d4f9a3b) that changes how route metadata is attached to stream resumes
sam: are the duplicate events identical? or is one provisional and one confirmed?
maria: one is flagged provisional:true and then later a confirmed charge comes in, but the provisional wasn't being reconciled away when the confirmed arrived so both stuck
ida: on the metrics side provisional charges hit meter.provisional.tokens and then confirmed writes to meter.tokens. our dashboard only sums both which double counts for the UI
leo: so two likely issues: router emits duplicate records on alias handoff, and billing pipeline doesn't dedupe provisional vs confirmed by (session, toolcall, nonce)
mike: quick grep in router logs shows a retry path that re-emits toolcall metadata when it sees alias mismatch, probably intended for durability but leaking into accounting
sam: short-term mitigation: do we have an idempotency key we can use? session_id+toolcall_id+resume_index should be stable. billing can ignore provisional if it sees a confirmed with same id within Xs
ida: agreed. SQL to reconcile current surplus: ```sql
SELECT session_id, toolcall_id, COUNT(*) as cnt, SUM(tokens_charged)
FROM billing_events
WHERE created_at > now()-interval '48 hours'
AND (event_type='provisional' OR event_type='confirmed')
GROUP BY session_id, toolcall_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```
maria: can someone add a temporary query to the console to show provisional vs confirmed by session so support can quickly identify affected customers?
leo: @ida can you add that to the Billing dashboard? also add a heatmap of routes — alias vs direct — to see if certain aliases are noisy
ida: on it. will add a new tile and pinned SQL. also adding an alert when provisional>confirmed ratio > 0.2 for a route
mike: long-term we should change router to avoid emitting synthetic toolcall events on fallback; instead attach a handoff marker to the original stream event
sam: I can draft a small change in billing to dedupe by idempotency key and to treat provisional as soft until a confirm or timeout. then cleanup job will remove stale provisionals after 24h
maria: leaving this with @sam and @ida for now. can we also surface a console flag to hide provisional charges from customer-facing quota UI until reconciliation? that'd reduce noise for SREs
sam: yes, will add feature flag f_hide_provisional_in_quota and wire it to the UI layer
ops-bot: incident-created: INC-2024-413 -> billing: provisional double-counting on alias handoff (assigned @sam @ida)
leo: thanks. can we also add a quick query for support: `SELECT * FROM billing_events WHERE session_id='s-42f' ORDER BY created_at;` so they can see the event chain
maria: perfect. after mitigation, let's do a postmortem and include recommended router invariants (no synthetic toolcall events, annotate instead). also add rollout guard for alias-handoff in canary
ida: scheduling a short sync in 30m to coordinate console tiles and reconciliation job
maria: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
